**Verdict: changes requested** - the PR body only; no code change is needed. The code passed the built review below.

Built and tested locally at this head, in a worktree, debug profile. I did not write this change. This is a P1 floor review (stock sim, gouge check); a second (Opus) review is still needed before a merge.

## Blocker

1. **The PR body is empty.** Pull Request Law: the body must state what changed, the readings, the pinning tests, what was not exercised, a `Changelog:` line, and end with `Fixes #2596`. Write the body; then the labels can move. No push is needed for this.

## Code: checked and correct

- The law matches the Done-means of #2596 in all three parts. A no-pick chamfer rides only the bevelled loops (`ride_loops`), a model with no bevel still breaks every top edge (#303 kept, `out.is_empty()` path), and an orphan bevelled rim in a sharp plate refuses by name with the spot (`GenError::At`).
- `auto_edges` is the right predicate: a chamfer with picks carries `SrcRef::Selection`; `SrcRef::Entity` is the whole model. A stock-edge chamfer keeps the `breaks_stock_edge` path.
- The verify side drops all edge-break credit when `models_a_bevel` finds a bevel on any declared record: `max(top -probe, top +probe) >= edge_z - tol` fails only where the model stands lower on both sides - at a sharp edge one side is the part top. Framed (`volume`) records and single points are excluded, as in `on_walls`. A non-finite edge length gives `None`, which is not credited and not a bevel: stricter, never looser.
- The `walled()` refactor keeps its condition identical (`min(sides) <= z - depth + tol`); only the sampler moved into `samples`.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests in the diff. Decision file `docs/decisions/2596-chamfer-sharp-edge.md` is present and records the dropped strict refusal and the parameter idea. No new crate edge: `app` already used `camcraft_sim::stock_sim`.

## Local results at `5e1a01eaa`

- `camcraft-sim --lib wall_anchor`: 4 pass, incl. `a_sharp_edge_carries_no_modelled_bevel` and `an_edge_with_the_model_below_it_on_both_sides_is_a_modelled_bevel`.
- `camcraft-motion --lib` (chamfer): 7 pass, incl. `a_sharp_pocket_beside_a_modelled_bevel_is_left_alone` and `a_bevelled_pocket_rim_inside_a_sharp_plate_refuses_by_name`.
- `camcraft-app --test chamfer_modelled_edge`: 7 pass, incl. the #2596 plate tests: clean ride posts with an empty gate; the old ride put back by hand is a gouge with a charged line.
- `camcraft-app --test edge_break_gate`: 5 pass - the #303 law is intact.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim`: clean. The app crates compiled for the test runs; app clippy was not run.

## Merge check

GitHub reports `MERGEABLE` (head based on `1613e42f9`).

## Non-blockers

- `crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs` is now 496 lines; main is already at 491. The +5 worsens an existing overrun, not a new break; a later split is welcome.
- #2596 notes "No note says which edges the op picked." The fix rides only the modelled edges but gives no user-visible edge list; only a `tracing::warn!` marks the credit drop. If we want a UI note, file a `P7` follow-up - not in this PR.

## Not checked

- No full-workspace build, no clippy on `camcraft-app`.
- Not exercised: a modelled ROUND (the code reads it as a bevel; only chamfers are tested), a part whose bevel is at a ledge below the top plane.

**Verdict: ready**

Read from the diff. Not built.

Opus second review of a P1 fix. I did not write this change. I read the first review by the SlaveSession and do not repeat its results.

## Blockers

None.

The blocker of the first review (an empty PR body) is closed. The body at this head has what changed, the pinning tests, "Not exercised", a `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #2596`. The `needs-rework` label is still on the PR. I did not change it.

## Checked

1. **Generator.** `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs` L54-106. A top loop with a gap of `SAME_EDGE` (1e-6 mm, plan) or less to its wall goes to `sharp`. A loop with a larger gap goes to `out` as before. If `out` is empty, the op rides all sharp loops (#303 law, L85-88). Else the sharp loops are not ridden. A bevelled loop can not go to `sharp`: its gap is the bevel width. Thus no modelled chamfer is skipped. The only caller is the no-pick path, `crates/app/src/operation/material_source.rs` L216-222. A user pick does not use `ride_loops` and is not changed. The orphan bevelled rim in a sharp plate is refused by name with `GenError::At` (L95-104). Islands and through holes follow the same loop rule. The section regions have no open loops.
2. **Verify.** The PR changes the judgement. `crates/app/src/stock_sim_breaks.rs` L139-151: a no-pick chamfer (`auto_edges`, L80-85, `SrcRef::Entity`) gets no edge-break credit when `models_a_bevel` is true. Then the cone is judged against the model, and a cut on a sharp edge is a gouge that blocks the post. `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/wall_anchor.rs` L62-73: the records are at `top_z` (`chamfer.rs` L148-156), and the probe is 0.05 mm (`WALL_PROBE`) to each side. A sharp edge has the part top on one side. A bevel has the model lower on the two sides. `tol` is clamped to finite and not negative. A non-finite edge length gives `None`, which is not a bevel. I agree with the first review that the `walled()` refactor keeps its condition. The old cached ride of #2596 has the outer bevel record, thus it also loses its credit.
3. **Tests.** `a_no_pick_chamfer_leaves_a_sharp_pocket_beside_a_modelled_chamfer_alone` (`chamfer_modelled_edge.rs` L248-259) asserts each tip on the outer wall at z 9, and a clean gate. On main the pocket rim is ridden, so it fails there. `a_no_pick_chamfer_cut_into_a_sharp_pocket_rim_is_a_gouge` (L261-294) asserts a gouge line. On main `on_walls` credits the rim, so it fails there. The assertion of `a_no_pick_chamfer_on_a_rectangular_pocket_stays_clean` (L211-222) is not changed. Only a comment is added, and the PR body states why (#303, follow-up #2634). No test is deleted or ignored. No golden and no snapshot PNG changed.
4. **Laws.** No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests. No new operation parameter. The decision entry records the dropped parameter. File lengths at this head: `chamfer_ride.rs` 202, `wall_anchor.rs` 236, `stock_sim_breaks.rs` 163, `chamfer_modelled_edge.rs` 294. `stock_sim.rs` is 496 (491 on main, as the first review says). The tests are in the correct crates. `Fixes #2596` is correct: the two parts of "Done means" are met for the plate of the issue.
5. **Merge.** `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 5e1a01eaa` is clean.

## Non-blockers

- **A loop that is bevelled on one side only.** I disagree in part with "the law matches the Done-means in all three parts". `gap` (`chamfer_ride.rs` L111-118) is the largest vertex gap of the loop. A rectangle with a modelled chamfer on one side and three sharp sides is one bevelled loop. The op rides its full wall loop, and the three sharp sides get a chamfer. This is not a silent gouge: `models_a_bevel` is true for that record, the credit is dropped, and the post is refused with a gouge. But the default op then makes a toolpath that verify refuses. I recommend a `P7` follow-up: classify sharp against bevelled for each span of a loop, not for each loop. This was also true on main.
- **A drafted wall.** A wall with a small draft has a gap larger than 1e-6 mm, thus it counts as a bevel. On a part with a drafted outer wall and a vertical pocket, the op now skips the pocket rim. The model has no modelled chamfer there. This is safe (less cut, no gouge), but the user does not see it. #2635 (P7, show the edges that the op skips) covers the visibility.
- **A bevel narrower than 0.05 mm.** `models_a_bevel` probes at 0.05 mm, so a modelled bevel narrower than that reads as sharp. The generator still skips the sharp rim. Only an old cached ride on such a part keeps its credit. Very small risk.
- **Rounds and other angles.** With the credit dropped, a no-pick ride is clean only where the cone matches the modelled face. A modelled round, a chamfer at a different angle from the tool, or a width larger than the modelled chamfer now gives a gouge at post. This is correct by the Prime Directive, but it changes what posts. A test with a round is not in the PR (the body says so).
- The refusal message (L98-101) gives the position of the first bevelled loop, not always the orphan loop.

## Not checked

- No build, no test run, no clippy. I rely on the first review for the local results.
- The reporter's project files.
- `Region::new` re-nesting rules, beyond the refusal test.

Merge by the merging session. Class: no refresh (the reviewed head is the merged head, `5e1a01eaa7610c9914dd4779a346190e5824f10d`).

Reviews that this merge relies on:
- the built review of this head (comment of 2026-11-18T23:33Z). Its one request was the PR body. It found no code blocker.
- the Opus second review of this head, verdict ready, required for a P1 fix: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2638#issuecomment-6994872959. It confirms that the body is complete now.

The main session reported that the first reviewer accepts the completed body. The `needs-rework` label is stale and I remove it after the merge. The PR is flagged ready now. Nothing is pushed after this flag.

**Verdict: ready**

Update of my built review at this head. The one blocker - the empty body - is resolved. The body now states what changed, the readings, the pinning tests, what was not exercised, a `Changelog:` line, and `Fixes #2596`. The test names in the body match the suites I ran green: sim 4, motion 7 (2 new), app `chamfer_modelled_edge` 7 and `edge_break_gate` 5, clippy clean on motion and sim. The head did not move; the code verdict is unchanged.

Follow-ups exist and are triaged: #2634 (the maintainer's decision on the strict reading of #2596) and #2635 (show the edges the op rides - the "no note" point of my review). The body's extra suites (edge_break_bound, setup_carry_credits, stock_source_holes, stock_chamfer_added_part, mill2d_b chamfer) are the author's results; I did not reproduce them.

**P1 floor: a second (Opus) read-only review is still needed before a merge.**
